## The Problem

Every 529-eligible purchase meant the same three manual steps: snap a photo of the receipt, log it in a shared spreadsheet, and email my dad a specifically formatted message so he could file it. I built an app to do all three in the time it takes to scan one photo.

My family tracks 529-eligible education expenses (food, textbooks, and similar) through a shared spreadsheet with my dad, and every receipt needs to reach him as an email with a specific subject line format so he can file it correctly. Doing that by hand for every single purchase — photo, spreadsheet entry, formatted email — got old fast and was easy to fall behind on.

## What I Built and Why

I built a PWA that scans a receipt photo, runs it through OCR to pull out the vendor, amount, and date, and auto-categorizes it against a list of 100+ known vendors (it also flags 529-eligible categories like food and textbooks automatically). Saving a receipt does three things at once: stores it in a Supabase database I can pull from anywhere, fires off an email to my dad with the receipt photo attached and the exact subject line format he needs, and adds it to an Excel export I can generate anytime with a 529-eligible column built in. I kept the frontend as vanilla JS with a couple of Python serverless functions on Vercel rather than reaching for a framework, since this only needed to solve one specific, well-scoped problem. I added PIN authentication later once I realized the app was reachable by anyone with the URL.

## How It Went

It collapsed three manual steps (photo, spreadsheet, formatted email) into one. I scan the receipt and the rest happens automatically.

## What I'd Do Differently

The OCR-to-data parsing held up better than I expected. Going back through the commit history, the "fixes" there were really just the vendor and category dictionaries growing as I added more stores, not the regex itself breaking. The actual fragile part was email delivery: getting Gmail to stop blocking the message and getting the subject line spacing exactly right for my dad's filing system took several rounds of trial and error, and left behind a lot of step-by-step debug logging I only recently went back and stripped out. If I rebuilt it, I'd write a couple of real tests around the email formatting up front instead of debugging it live.

## Tech Stack

Vanilla HTML/CSS/JS, Python Flask (Vercel serverless functions), Supabase (PostgreSQL), OCR.space, Gmail SMTP, SheetJS, Vercel hosting
